headline: Colts 24, Dolphins 22

body.label: The result
body.text: Miami went into Indianapolis and lost by two, 24–22. The Dolphins had it close into the fourth quarter and still walked out with nothing — their eighth loss of the year.

body.label: Where it stands
body.text: At 1–8, the math is what it is. Half a season gone and one tally in the win column. This group keeps finding new ways to come up a possession short.

body.label: Big Sarge's take
body.text: Two points on the road. I’ve watched this team lose ugly and I’ve watched it lose close, and close is the one that eats at you — because it means the talent is there and the finish isn’t. You don’t get credit for almost in this league. Fix the fourth quarter or keep losing it.

hurricanes.headline: No. 7 Miami 36, Duke 25

body.label: Turning points
body.text: With Miami clinging to a 22–17 lead, freshman Javian Mallory capped a 79-yard drive with a touchdown. Xavier Lucas then picked off Walker Eget, and Mallory put it away with a 39-yard scoring run.

body.label: Standouts
body.text: Mallory went for 150 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns. Darian Mensah threw for 382 yards and Cooper Barkate hauled in eight catches for 134. Mark Fletcher Jr.’s 36th career rushing touchdown set a new Miami record.

body.label: Injury news
body.text: Fletcher left with a lower-body injury but is expected back against Virginia Tech, as is safety Zechariah Poyser. Malachi Toney remains out after ankle surgery — ahead of schedule, but likely unavailable until a possible ACC Championship appearance.

body.label: Big Sarge's take
body.text: Five hundred and thirty-two yards, 7–0 in the league, and one win from an ACC title berth — that’s a season most programs would kill for. But another scoreless first quarter, 10 penalties, and two red-zone trips that netted field goals instead of six? Talent’s carrying them. Discipline had better catch up before it costs them the one that matters.
